status: exploratory (pre-registered criterion and choice rule; Phase 11 calibration of the one model that passed Phase 9)
hypothesis: The E012 1h move-size model's stated probabilities are already close to honest (uncalibrated ECE 0.013 exploration / 0.040 validation). A calibrator fitted on a purged, most-recent 90-day slice of each fold's training range can correct the residual drift (2024-25 is calmer than the training years, so the raw model should over-state the chance of a large move) without destroying the model's ranking ability.
what_is_calibrated: P(|return over the next 1h| > 0.25%) from the E012 1h model (same nine inputs, same log transforms, L2 logistic C = 0.1, expanding walk-forward). Direction is NOT calibrated: E011 found no directional signal, so the honest direction probability is the base rate, stated as such.

variants.raw: the model's own logistic output; the calibration slice is reserved but unused, so all three variants train on identical rows and are scored on identical test rows
variants.platt: 1-parameter-pair logistic recalibration a*logit(p)+b fitted on the calibration slice
variants.isotonic: monotone step function fitted on the calibration slice (sklearn IsotonicRegression, clipped outside the fitted range)

validation_design: expanding walk-forward, min_train 365d, calibration slice = the last 90 days of each training range, purge = 1h + 24h embargo on BOTH sides of the slice (fit rows | purge | calibration rows | purge | test block), quarterly test blocks, identical folds for all three variants (first test block therefore starts ~90 days later than in E012)
acceptance_criterion: PRE-REGISTERED. Evaluated on the concatenated out-of-sample test rows. (C1) 'Calibrated' in the VALIDATION period (2024-01 -> 2025-06) means: ECE (10 equal-width buckets, size-weighted) <= 0.03 AND every bucket with >= 100 rows has |observed frequency - mean stated probability| <= 0.05. Exploration-period values are reported alongside. (C2) Ranking preserved: Spearman rho(p, realised |return|) in validation within 0.02 of the raw model's. (C3) CHOICE RULE, fixed in advance: among the variants meeting C1 and C2, take the SIMPLEST (raw, then Platt, then isotonic) unless a more complex one lowers validation Brier by at least 1% relative to the simpler one. If no variant meets C1, the output stays labelled 'uncalibrated heuristic' and this is recorded as a fail. The sealed holdout (2025-07 -> 2026-08) is not touched; it will judge the chosen variant once, in Phase 12.
tripwire: Validation ECE < 0.005 for any variant, or a Brier improvement over raw larger than 5% relative, is treated as suspicious (a calibrator cannot add information; it can only re-map probabilities) and investigated before being recorded.

target.outcome: close of the candle opening at as_of + 1h

periods.calibration: last 90 days of each fold's training range, purged on both sides

hyperparameters.platt: LogisticRegression on logit(p), C = 1e6 (effectively unregularised), 2 parameters

metrics.first_test_block: 2018-11-27 15:00 (90 days later than E012, as pre-declared)
metrics.calibration_rows_per_fold: 1,584-2,160 (90 days minus hours blanked by the no-fill rule)
metrics.fold_gaps_hours: 26 on 25 folds; 29 and 85 on two folds with data holes (never below the required 26)

results: Raw FAILS C1 in validation (ECE 0.043, one bucket 0.06 off): in 2024-25 the raw model UNDER-states the chance of a large move (mean stated 0.434 vs observed 0.475) -- the opposite direction from the hypothesis. PLATT PASSES C1 and C2 (validation ECE 0.014, every bucket with >= 100 rows within 0.03; rho 0.360 vs raw 0.362); its intercept drifts from about -0.2 in early folds to +0.2 in the latest, i.e. it tracks the regime shift the raw model misses. ISOTONIC FAILS C1 (worst bucket 0.10 off in validation, 0.145 in exploration; log loss much worse because it emits exact 0/1 from a 90-day slice). Brier: Platt 0.7% better than raw in validation, isotonic 0.3% -- both under the 1% 'complexity justified' bar, which does not matter here because raw fails C1 outright.
chosen_variant: PLATT -- by the pre-registered rule: the simplest variant meeting C1 and C2 (raw fails C1; isotonic fails C1). Per-year ECE <= 0.03 in all 8 years (0.008-0.029).
consistent_across_time: Platt has the lowest ECE in 7 of 8 years and is within 0.001 of the best in the 8th; raw's ECE is worst in exactly the regime-shift years (2021, 2024, 2025). Ranking ability (rho) is unchanged by calibration in every period, as it must be.
leakage_check: Calibrator sees only the purged 90-day slice (unit test with a recording calibrator); fit rows | 25h | calibration rows | 25h | test rows on every fold; test blocks identical across the three variants; the tripwires (ECE < 0.005 in validation, Brier gain > 5%) did not fire. Exploration ECE of 0.0044 for Platt is an average over 41k rows and 23 folds, consistent with an honest re-map, not with information leaking in.
overfitting_suspected: Isotonic: yes (step function on ~2,000 rows produces extreme buckets and exact 0/1 outputs) -- rejected by the rule. Platt: 2 parameters per fold, stable (a 0.89-1.13, b -0.21 to +0.22): no.
affected_design: The research deliverable is now: P(|next-hour move| > 0.25%) = Platt(E012 logistic), refit quarterly with a purged 90-day calibration slice. This is what Phase 12 will judge once on the sealed holdout. The live system's confidence number stays the labelled heuristic; wiring the calibrated probability into it is a separate decision after Phase 12/13, never a research side-effect.
notes: Three runs (raw / platt / isotonic), all reported. Whatever is chosen is a research artefact: the live system's confidence stays the labelled heuristic until a separate, validated decision wires the move-size probability into it.
